name: Yansi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Rottland, Franz. 1970. Die Verbformen des Yanzi (dissertation on Yansi verb morphology, likely with phonological sketch); also Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015 lexicon cited on Glottolog. Neither online

sources.citation: Kasiangula Bulukani, Bertin & Jacques Nkiene Musinga. 2026. La morphophonologie du kiyansi, langue bantu B85b (Mikwi, RD Congo). Revue-IRS 4(3): 5770-5788. doi:10.5281/zenodo.21035174.
sources.note: No Yansi-specific stress statement; Part II is morphotonology (tonal harmony/contrast/contraction/inversion/spreading). Sec. 3.6 (p. 5781) quotes Nkiene (2017:30) listing generic zone-B traits including 'la forte tendance a l'accent dynamique sur la penultieme' -- second-hand areal remark, not a description of Yansi.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Yansi (yns): 5 datapoints, all from Mayanga 1985 (Grammaire yansi), none on stress (features 14A-17A absent).
sources.note: No stress features coded for Yansi.

sources.citation: Rottland, Franz. 1977. Reflexes of Proto-Bantu phonemes in Yanzi (B.85). Africana Linguistica 7: 375-396. doi:10.3406/aflin.1977.906 (Persee).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. B.5 (p. 378): suprasegmentals are vowel length and three tonemes (high, low, downstep); no mention of stress/accent anywhere in the 22 pages (text layer + Persee scanned grepped).

sources.citation: Kasiangula Bulukani, Bertin. 2026. Creation lexicale par reduplication en kiyansi, langue bantu B85b (Mikwi, RD Congo). Revue Internationale de la Recherche Scientifique (Revue-IRS) 4(2): 3316-3331. doi:10.5281/zenodo.20036907.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3 'Phonologie synchronique et tonale du kiyansi de Mikwi' (pp. 3318-3323): 10 vowels, 17 consonants + 2 glides, closed syllables, tones H, L, falling, rising; 'Le ton est pertinent en Kiyansi de Mikwi'. No accent/stress statement.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara et al. 2025. Language divergence and convergence and deep-time population history in the Kwilu-Kasai region (UGent biblio 01K0KHBZ1PEASPFHMQRZFJ4Z95).
Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437-475. doi:10.1163/19552629-14020007.
sources.note: No stress statement for Yans; says final vowel loss is 'not phonologically and/or prosodically determined or constrained'; useful list of Yans sources (Swartenbroeckx 1948, Mufwene 1973, Rottland 1977, Nguma-Nanzioke 1983, Koni Muluwa & Bostoen 2015).

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara, Natalia Chousou-Polydouri & Koen Bostoen. 2019. Untangling the West-Coastal Bantu mess: identification, geography and phylogeny of the Bantu B50-80 languages. Africana Linguistica 25: 155-229.
sources.note: Classification paper; PDF text layer font-garbled, partially decoded; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph & Koen Bostoen. 2012. La diphtongaison dans les langues bantu B70-80 (Bandundu, RDC): typologie et classification historique. Africana Linguistica 18: 355-386 (Persee).
sources.note: Nothing on accent; Yans is one of 13 languages surveyed for diphthongization.

sources.citation: Daeleman, Jan. 1977. A comparative study of some zone B languages in Bantu. Africana Linguistica 7: 93-143 (Persee).
sources.note: Nothing; Yans data second-hand from Swartenbroeckx 1948, explicitly 'lack of tonal data for Yans'.

sources.note: Phonology-and-morphology sketch of the Ntsambaan (B85F) variety filed under yans1239; Congolese memoires of this school usually include a paragraph on 'accent'.

sources.citation: Nkiene Musinga, Jacques. 2021. Elements d'etude des langues africaines: phonologie et morphologie du bantu. Kikwit: Ed. Diba (ISP-Kikwit), 240 pp.; and Nkiene M. 2017. 'Consonne en situation de C2 en bantu', Pistes et Recherches 33(1): 8-21 (ISP-Kikwit).

sources.note: Source of the second-hand 'accent dynamique sur la penultieme' zone-B remark quoted in Kasiangula & Nkiene 2026; Nkiene works on Kwilu B80 languages incl. Kiyansi and may state the Yansi accent facts first-hand.

sources.citation: Koni Muluwa, Joseph & Koen Bostoen. 2015. Lexique compare des langues bantu du Kwilu (RDC). Koln: Koppe. 197 pp. (hdl.handle.net/1854/LU-7030182, UGent only)

sources.note: Modern fieldwork-based source cited by Glottolog for Yansi; transcription/phonology introduction may state the accentual pattern (stem-initial prominence) of the Kwilu B80 languages including Yans and Nsambaan.

sources.citation: Mayanga, Tayeye. 1985. Grammaire yansi (Rep. du Zaire). (Publications CEEBA, serie III.) Bandundu: Centre d'Etudes Ethnologiques de Bandundu. 162 pp.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only full grammar of Yansi (Glottolog hhtype grammar; WALS's source); its phonology chapter is the most likely place for an explicit statement on accent/stress vs tone.

sources.note: Contrastive Yansi-English phonology by a native-speaker linguist; interference section likely comments on English stress vs Yansi prosody.
